subject: Open-Model Readiness: Curelytics discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Park <alexandra@curelytics.ai>, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@curelytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Open-Model Readiness: Curelytics discovery recap & next steps

Hi Alexandra / Tom —

Thanks again for carving out 30 minutes today. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment and clear next steps. I tried to keep this short and actionable.

Summary of your pain / triggers
- Heavy dependence on OpenAI for clinical summarization and diagnostic-assist features; spend is rising and token costs are unpredictable.
- Latency spikes during peak ingest windows (affects UAT experience and some real-time workflows).
- Data residency & audit trails requirement for customer contracts (SOC2 + logs for model inputs/outputs).
- Occasional factual errors / hallucinations in summaries — clinical QA currently requires manual passes.

Current stack you described
- UI & orchestration on AWS ECS; ingestion pipeline -> preprocessor -> completion calls.
- Primary models: OpenAI gpt-4o for summarization and Anthropic Claude for safety/post-filtering.
- Custom reranker (in-house) for top-N selection and a lightweight embedding-based cache for common prompts.

Success criteria you listed
- Quality parity: clinical summary accuracy at or above current baseline (we agreed to pilot with a 200-record sample).
- Latency: p50 < 350ms for standard patient-summary calls; p95 targets to be discussed.
- Throughput: sustain ~100 req/s in peak window without degrading latency SLA.
- Compliance: VPC deployment option, request/response audit logs, support for your KMS.
- Cost objective: reduce per-1M-token spend by >= 30% (goal for evaluation).

Initial compatibility & gaps we noted
- Prompts and post-processing will need small adjustments; most schema-based outputs should port cleanly.
- Your safety step using Claude would likely map to a lightweight local safety model + rule-based checks; we can prototype with a smaller safety model.
- Embedding and reranker compatibility should be straightforward; we'll validate embedding vector dims and retrain the reranker if needed.

Model shortlist / experiments we proposed
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (quantized) – strong instruction following, low-cost baseline for batch jobs.
- Llama-2-Chat (70B, int8/quantized) – quality target for parity; evaluate on the 200-record sample.
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (optimized quant) – middle ground for latency/cost tradeoff.
- Fallback: keep OpenAI/Anthropic for high-sensitivity or hard regressions during rollout.

Suggested next steps (we agreed on timeline)
1) I will send two artifacts by EOD: (a) a short discovery notes PDF and (b) rough MAU/cost estimate workbook.
2) You to share the 200-record anonymized sample + current prompt set by EOD Monday (Nov 2).
3) Marissa (cc'd) to run an infra feasibility call with your infra lead next week to scope VPC/KMS needs.
4) Schedule a 60-min pilot kickoff after we confirm sample receipt (target week of Nov 9).

If I missed anything or mis-stated priorities, please flag and I’ll update. Appreciate the transparency — we’ll aim to have an initial proof-of-concept that hits your quality bar before any large cutover decisions.

Attachments: curelytics-discovery-notes.pdf, mau-and-cost-estimates.xlsx

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0123 | diego@redwood.ai

From: Alexandra Park <alexandra@curelytics.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@curelytics.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Open-Model Readiness: Curelytics discovery recap & next steps

Diego —

Appreciate the concise write-up, this looks correct. A couple clarifications:
- The 200-record sample will be de-identified PHI (we'll scrub names but keep structure and clinical terms).
- Latency target: p50 < 350ms is right; p95 target we set as < 1.1s for the pilot.
- On cost: the 30% reduction is aspirational; we want to see realistic ranges for different model families.

I’ll aim to get the sample and prompt set to you by close of business Monday. Tom will coordinate our infra lead (Megan) for the VPC/KMS call — I’ve included her on the calendar invite tentatively.

Quick question for Redwood: how do you handle audit-log retention for private deployments? We have tiered retention based on customer SLAs (30/90/365 days).

Thanks,
Alexandra Park
Head of Product, Curelytics
alexandra@curelytics.ai

Thanks Alex — good questions. Quick answers inline and a couple of operational notes: 

> how do you handle audit-log retention for private deployments?
We support configurable retention policies for audit logs in Private: customer-configured windows (30/90/365) and export hooks to S3/GCS. For VPC we can map logs to your KMS and provide signed delivery receipts. We’ll detail options in the infra call.

Operational notes:
- Attached discovery PDF includes the short evaluation matrix and suggested metric scripts (ROUGE + clinical exact-match heuristics).
- Cost workbook has two scenarios: conservative (higher-quality, larger models) and pragmatic (mixed small/medium quantized models).
- If you can share the sample by Monday EOD, Marissa will spin up a small internal eval (no charge) and we’ll return results within 5 business days.

Proposed meeting: Pilot kickoff (60m) — Wed Nov 11 @ 10:00 AM PT. Please confirm or suggest alternatives.

Thanks again — looking forward to running the pilot.

Diego
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
